text:
Alex R: Proposing a new GPU node pool in us-south1 to handle inference for our LatAm customers. Primary needs: H100 capacity for large-context generation (low latency) and a separate A10G pool for embeddings / low-priority batch. Want opinions on sizing, quota risk, and whether to use preemptible/spot for A10G.

Priya K: What's the traffic profile (steady vs spiky)? also where are we on regional GPU quotas today?

Alex R: Steady ~30 qps for gen models (avg 6-12 tokens), spikes up to ~120 qps for short windows. Latency SLO 95th <250ms. We’d like scale-up within ~3m for spikes. Quota looks low in us-south1 right now.

Jamie L: For that burstiness we should run H100s as reserved (min 1 warm node) and A10Gs as spot with autoscale. Suggest config: H100 pool: min=1 max=12, 1 GPU/node, tainted (inference=dedicated:NoSchedule), label pool=us-south1-h100. A10G pool: min=0 max=20, 1 GPU/node, spot.

Maria (infra): FYI quota in region is currently 0/4 H100 allocated. I submitted quota request Q-4021 to Cloud (https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=redwood&q=Q-4021). Will escalate if they ask for justification.

Alex R: Do we want to try multi-gpu nodes (2x GPUs) to reduce per-node overhead? Concern is pod packing and OOM for KV cache. Prefer 1 GPU/node for predictable latency.

Jamie L: Agree 1 GPU/node simplifies scheduling and eviction. Also recommend disabling binpack-similar-node-groups in CA profile so it can mix instance types if needed. Increase cluster-autoscaler parallelism to help fast ramp (scale-up-limit 3 nodes at once).

Maria (infra): Draft gcloud snippet for H100 pool (will validate machine-type with cloud before apply):
```
# create H100 pool (placeholder machine-type)
gcloud container node-pools create us-south1-h100 \ 
  --cluster=prod-cluster \ 
  --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g \ 
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-h100,count=1 \ 
  --num-nodes=0 \ 
  --min-nodes=1 \ 
  --max-nodes=12 \ 
  --node-labels=pool=us-south1-h100,role=inference \ 
  --node-taints=inference=dedicated:NoSchedule \ 
  --enable-autoscaling
```

And for A10G (spot):
```
# spot A10G pool
gcloud container node-pools create us-south1-a10g-spot \ 
  --cluster=prod-cluster \ 
  --machine-type=n1-highmem-8 \ 
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \ 
  --num-nodes=0 \ 
  --min-nodes=0 \ 
  --max-nodes=20 \ 
  --spot \ 
  --node-labels=pool=us-south1-a10g,role=embeddings \ 
  --enable-autoscaling
```

Priya K: Two quick asks: (1) file a cost estimate for monthly baseline+burst (so finance can pre-approve); (2) add podDisruptionBudget and PDB-aware rollout so drains don't spike tail latencies.

Alex R: I'll sketch a rough cost note. If H100 on-demand is ~ $X/hr, baseline min=1 + avg scaled 4 nodes during peak windows -> rough monthly O(ten-thousands). We should consider short-term reserved commitment if we see steady use.

Jamie L: Also watch out for quota fragmentation: requesting 20 H100s will be a red flag. Start with request for 12 and plan to increase after initial metrics. 

Maria (infra): Filed Q-4021 for 12 H100s and Q-4022 for 20 A10Gs. Ticket notes included expected throughput, business justification, and traffic windows. Paging @cloud-quotas to speed up.

sre-bot: [alert] last autoscaler event: scale-up duration 7m 12s for previous pool (prod-west). See dashboard: https://go/infra/ca-events/1955

Alex R: 7m is too slow for our SLO. Options: keep min=1 warm H100 node (ensures <1m cold start), use node-provisioning warmers, or rely on a small local cache to absorb spikes.

Jamie L: If we set min=1 then cost of idle H100 is unavoidable. Alternative: run a small fleet of smaller CPU nodes with a local L2 cache to avoid full model cold starts — but complexity is higher. For now let's trial min=1 for 72h and measure.

Priya K: Agree on trial. Also make sure RBAC/taints allow evictions and node draining gracefully. Add a canary rollout for one customer region first.

Maria (infra): Plan: 1) request quotas (Q-4021/4022) - in flight; 2) create A10G spot pool (min=0) today for embeddings; 3) create H100 pool with min=1 once quota approved; 4) run 72h trial, collect CA scale metrics and tail latency. I'll open infra PR with the gcloud YAML and a short runbook.

Alex R: Sounds good. Assigning action items: Maria -> infra PR + quota follow-up; Priya -> cost estimate and PDBs; Jamie -> autoscaler tuning (scale-up limits, parallelism); Alex -> canary plan and metrics.

Maria (infra): On it. Tagging this thread to keep updates here. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [note] create follow-up incident if scale-up time >5m during trial.

Alex R: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after quota reply or first deploy.
